61:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Saff Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, who said: We were discussing which of you would go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ask him which deeds are most beloved to God. None of us got up, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent a man to us, and he gathered us and recited to us this Surah, meaning the entire Surah As-Saff. This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid bin Mazid Al-Bayrouti told us, reciting, he said: My father told me, I heard Al-Awza’i tell me, Yahya bin Abi Katheer tell me, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman tell me, Abdullah bin Salam tell me that some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If we were to send to the Messenger of God to ask him about the most beloved deeds to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, none of us would go to him, and we were afraid to ask him about that. He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called those people, man by man, until he gathered them, and this Surah was revealed about them: Glorify God Al-Saff. Abdullah bin Salam said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it all to us. Abu Salamah said: Abdullah ibn Salam recited it all to us. Yahya ibn Abi Katheer said: Abu Salamah recited it all to us. Al-Awza’i said: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer recited it all to us. My father said: Al-Awza’i recited it all to us. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi: Muhammad ibn Katheer told us on the authority of al-Awza’i on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam who said: A group of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sat and talked, then we said: If we knew which deeds are most beloved to God, the Almighty, we would do them. Then God revealed: “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do?” Abdullah ibn Salam said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) recited it to us. Abu Salamah said: Ibn Salam recited it to us. Yahya said: Abu Salamah recited it to us. Ibn Katheer said: Al-Awza’i recited it to us. Abdullah said: Ibn Katheer recited it to us. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Kathir was contradicted in the chain of transmission of this hadith on the authority of Al-Awza’i. Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated on the authority of Al-Awza’i on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Kathir on the authority of Hilal ibn Abi Maymunah on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam or on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam. I said: Imam Ahmad narrated it in this way on the authority of Ya’mar on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak. Al-Tirmidhi said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated this hadith on the authority of Al-Awza’i similar to the narration of Muhammad ibn Kathir. I said: Al-Walid ibn Yazid narrated it in this way on the authority of Al-Awza’i as Ibn Kathir narrated it. I said: This hadith was told to me by the Sheikh, the Musnad, Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abi Talib Al-Hijjar, who read it to me while I was listening. Abu Al-Munja Abdullah ibn Umar ibn Al-Lati informed us. Abu Al-Waqt Abdul-Awal ibn Isa ibn Shu’ayb Al-Sajzi informed us. He said: Abu Al-Hasan ibn Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Muzaffar ibn Muhammad ibn Dawud Al-Dawudi informed us. Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamwiyah Al-Sarakhsi informed us. Isa ibn Imran Al-Samarqandi informed us. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman Al-Darimi informed us in its entirety. Muhammad bin Kathir informed us on the authority of Al-Awza’i, and he mentioned with his chain of transmission something similar. Its recitation was transmitted to us in a chain of transmission to our Sheikh Abu Al-Abbas Al-Hijjar, but he did not recite it because he was illiterate, and there was not enough time to teach it to him, but the great Hafiz Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Uthman Al-Dhahabi, may God have mercy on him, informed me. Judge Taqi Al-Din bin Sulayman bin Al-Shaykh Abu Umar informed us. Abu Al-Munja bin Al-Lati informed us, and he mentioned it with his chain of transmission, and it was transmitted to me in a chain of transmission through his path, and he recited it to me in its entirety, and praise and thanks be to God. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed the verse: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise more than once, so there is no need to repeat it. The verse: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? is a censure of the one who makes a promise or says something that he does not fulfill. For this reason, some of the early scholars who held the view that a promise must be fulfilled in all cases, whether the person who made the promise intended it or not, used this noble verse as evidence. They also cited as evidence from the Sunnah what was proven in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he makes a promise he breaks it; when he speaks he lies; and when he is entrusted he betrays.” And in another hadith in the Sahih, There are four characteristics, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has one characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up. Among them, he mentioned breaking a promise. We have discussed these two hadith in detail at the beginning of his commentary on Al-Bukhari, all praise and gratitude be to God. For this reason, God the Almighty emphasized this censure of them when He said: Most hateful it is in the sight of God that you say what you do not do. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amir bin Rabi’ah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us when I was a boy. I went out to play, and my mother said: O Abdullah, come here, I will give you something. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: And what did you want to give him? She said: Dates. He said: If you had not done so, a lie would have been written against you. Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him, held that if a promise is linked to a penalty on the one who made the promise, then it is obligatory to fulfill it, as if he said to someone else, Get married and I will pay you such-and-such every day, and he got married, then he is obligated to give him what he deserved as long as he was like that, because it is a human right that is based on constraint. The majority held that it is not obligatory at all, and they interpreted the verse as having been revealed when they wished for jihad to be obligatory upon them, but when it was imposed, some of them refused it, as God Almighty said: “Have you not seen those to whom it was said, ‘Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah?’ But when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party of them feared the people as they feared God or even more, and they said, ‘Our Lord, why did You prescribe fighting for us? Why have You not delayed us for a short term?’ Say, ‘The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears God. And you will not be wronged a thread. Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were within fortified towers.’” God Almighty said: “And those who believe say, ‘Why was a surah not sent down?’ But when a decisive surah is sent down and fighting is mentioned therein, you will see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with a look of one fainting from death.” Thus, the meaning of this verse is as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? He said: Before jihad was made obligatory, some of the believers used to say, We would like God the Almighty to show us the most beloved deeds to Him so that we can do them. So God informed His Prophet that the most beloved deeds are belief in Him without doubt, and jihad against those who disobey Him, who contradicted the faith and did not acknowledge it. So when jihad was revealed, some of the believers disliked that and found it difficult to do so God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? This is the choice of Ibn Jarir. And Muqatil bin Hayyan said: The believers said, If we knew the most beloved deeds to God, we would do them. So God showed them the most beloved deeds to Him and said: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks. So He made it clear to them, and they were tested on the Day of Uhud, so they turned away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God the Almighty revealed regarding that: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? And He said: The most beloved of you to Me is he who fights in My cause. Some of them say: It was revealed about fighting, so a man might say: I fought, but he did not fight back; I stabbed, but he did not stab; I struck, but he did not strike; I was patient, but he did not be patient. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed as a rebuke to a people who used to say: We killed, we struck, we stabbed, and we did such and such, but they did not do them. Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed about a group of hypocrites who used to promise the Muslims victory but did not fulfill that promise. Malik said on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: Why do you say what you do not do? He said: About jihad. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: “Why do you say what you do not do? Great is hatred in the sight of God that you say what you do not do. Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure.” In between that, it was about a group of the Ansar, among them Abdullah ibn Rawahah, who said in a gathering: If we knew which deeds were most beloved to God, we would do them until we die. So God revealed this about them, and Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: I will not leave being imprisoned in the cause of God until I die. So he was killed as a martyr. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Furwah ibn Abi Al-Mughra told us, Ali ibn Masahr told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Abi Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad Al-Dailami, on the authority of his father, who said: Abu Musa sent for the reciters of the people of Basra, and three hundred men entered upon him, all of whom had recited the Qur’an. He said: You are the reciters of the people of Basra and the best of them. He said: We used to recite a surah which we likened to one of the Mus-bahis, but we forgot it, except that I have memorized from it: O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? So it will be a testimony written around your necks and you will be asked about it on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason God the Almighty said: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as if they were a solid structure. This is God’s notification of His love for His believing servants when they stand in ranks facing the enemies of God in the heat of battle, fighting in the cause of God against those who disbelieve in God, so that the word of God is supreme and His religion is the apparent and superior to all other religions. Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Abdullah told us, Hisham told us, Mujalid told us, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three at whom God laughs: a man who gets up at night, the people when they line up for prayer, and the people when they line up for battle.” Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Mujalid, on the authority of Abu al-Wadak, Jabr ibn Nawf, with it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu’aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told us, al-Aswad, meaning Ibn Shaiban, told us, Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shakheer told me, he said: Mutraf said: I heard a hadith from Abu Dharr that I longed to meet, so I met him and said: O Abu Dharr, I heard a hadith from you and I longed to meet you. He said: May God be your father, I have met you, so tell me. I said: I heard from you that you claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told you that God hates three and loves three. He said: Yes, I do not think I would lie about my close friend, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: So who are these three whom God Almighty loves? He said: A man fought in the cause of God, went out seeking reward and striving, and he encountered the enemy and was killed. You will find this in the revealed Book of God. Then he recited: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as if they were a solid structure. And he mentioned the hadith thus. He narrated this hadith from this source with this context and this wording, and he abbreviated it. At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mansur ibn al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Rib’i ibn Harash, on the authority of Zayd ibn Dhibyan, on the authority of Abu Dharr, with a more detailed and complete version than this. We have narrated it in another place, praise be to God. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: God the Almighty says to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: "My servant, the trusting, the chosen one, is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets, nor does he repay evil for evil, but pardons and forgives. His birth is in Mecca, his migration is in Tabah, his kingdom is in Syria, and his nation is the praisers, they praise God in every situation, and in every position they have a buzz like the buzzing of bees in the sky at dawn. They wash their limbs and tie their belts around their waists, their rows in battle are like their rows in prayer." Then he recited: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure. Shepherds of the sun pray the prayer wherever it catches them, even if they are on the back of an animal. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding God's statement: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, would not fight the enemy unless he stood in rows with them, and this is a teaching from God to the believers. He said: The Almighty’s saying: As if they were a solid structure means that some of them are stuck to some of the ranks in battle. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Some of them are stuck to some. Ibn Abbas said: As if they were a solid structure is fixed and does not move, stuck to some of them. Qatada said, As if they were a solid structure. Have you not seen how the owner of the structure does not like his structure to be different? Likewise, God, the Almighty, does not like His command to be different. God has lined up the believers in their battle and in their prayer. So adhere to the command of God, for it is a protection for those who adhere to it. All of this was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said, “Saeed bin Amr Al-Sakuni told me, Baqiyah bin Al-Waleed told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Maryam, on the authority of Yahya bin Jabir Al-Ta’i, on the authority of Abu Bahriya, who said, ‘They disliked fighting on horses and preferred fighting on the ground, because God, the Almighty, said, “Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks as if they were a solid structure.”’” He said, Abu Bahriya used to say, ‘If you see me turning around in the ranks, then come to my beard.’

They wash their limbs and tie their belts around their waists, their rows in battle are like their rows in prayer." 61:5: God Almighty says, informing us about His servant, His Messenger, and His interlocutor, Moses, son of Imran, peace be upon him, that he said to his al-Nas 114:Why do you harm me while you know that I am the Messenger of God to you? That is, you did not harm me while you know my truthfulness in the message that I brought to you. And in this is consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he suffered from the infidels of his people and others, and he was commanded to be patient. For this reason, he said, “May God have mercy on Moses: he was harmed with more than this, but he was patient.” And in it is a prohibition for the believers to attack the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or cause him harm, as God the Almighty said, O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God. And His statement, the Almighty, But when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. That is, when they turned away from following the truth despite their knowledge of it, God caused their hearts to deviate from guidance and filled them with doubt, confusion, and failure, as God the Almighty said, And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression wandering blindly. And God the Almighty said, “And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.” For this reason, God the Almighty said in this verse, And God does not… He guides the wicked people. God the Almighty said: “And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, ‘O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a Messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.’” Meaning, the Torah gave good tidings of me, and I am the confirmation of what it had informed about, and I am the bearer of good tidings of the one who will come after me, who is the Messenger, the unlettered Arab Prophet from Mecca, Ahmad. So Jesus, peace be upon him, is the Seal of the Prophets of the Children of Israel, and he lived among the leaders of the Children of Israel giving good tidings of Muhammad, who is Ahmad, the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, after whom there is no message or prophethood. How beautiful is the hadith that Al-Bukhari narrated in it, in which he said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im told me, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say, “I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi by whom God will wipe out disbelief, I am Al-Hashir, at whose feet mankind will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Mas’udi told us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abu Musa who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave himself names, some of which we have memorized. He said: I am Muhammad, and I am Ahmad, the Gatherer, the Returned, the Prophet of Mercy, Repentance, and the Great Battle. Muslim narrated it on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah with this same name. God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel (al-An’am 11:17). And God the Almighty said: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said: ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My covenant?’ They said: ‘We have acknowledged it.’ He said: ‘Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.’” Ibn Abbas said: God did not send a prophet without taking a covenant from him that if Muhammad were sent while he was alive, they would follow him, and he took a covenant from his nation that if Muhammad were sent while they were alive, they would follow him and support him. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to me on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan on the authority of the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they said: O Messenger of God, tell us about yourself. He said: “The supplication of my father Abraham and the good report of Jesus. My mother saw when she became pregnant with me as if a light had come out of her that illuminated the palaces of Busra in the land of Ash-Sham.” This is a good chain of narration, and corroborating evidence has been narrated for it from other sources. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Muawiyah ibn Salih narrated to us on the authority of Saeed ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Hilal al-Sulami on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, I am the Seal of the Prophets in the sight of God, and Adam was still kneading in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of that: the supplication of my father Abraham, the good report of Jesus, and the vision that my mother saw. And thus do the mothers of the prophets see.” Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, al-Faraj ibn Fadalah narrated to us, Luqman ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said: O Messenger of God, what was the beginning of your affair? He said, "The supplication of my father Abraham and the good report of Jesus. My mother saw that a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Damascus." Ahmad also said: Hasan bin Musa told us, I heard Khadij, the brother of Zuhair bin Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent us to the Negus, and we were about eighty men, including Abdullah bin Masoud, Ja’far, Abdullah bin Rawahah, Uthman bin Maz’un, and Abu Musa. We went to the Negus and the Quraysh had sent Amr bin Al-’As and Ammarah bin Al-Walid with a gift. When they entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him, then they rushed to his right and left and said to him: Some of our cousins have settled in your land and have abandoned us and our religion. He said: Where are they? They said: They are in your land, so send for them. So he sent for them. Ja’far said: I am your orator today. They followed him and he greeted them but did not prostrate. They said to him: Why do you not prostrate to the king? He said: We do not prostrate except to God, the Almighty. He said: Why is that? He said: God sent His Messenger to us and he commanded us not to prostrate to anyone except God Almighty and he commanded us to pray and give zakat. Amr ibn al-'As said: They disagree with you about Jesus, son of Mary. He said: What do you say about Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother? He said: We say as God, the Almighty, said: He is the Word of God and His Spirit which He bestowed upon the pure Virgin, who was not touched by a human being and who did not have a son. He said: Then he picked up a stick from the ground and said: O people of Abyssinia, priests, and monks, by God, they do not add anything to what we say about him that is equal to this. Welcome to you and to those from whom you have come. I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one whom Jesus, son of Mary, gave good tidings of. Descend wherever you wish. By God, were it not for the kingdom I hold, I would have come to him and carried his sandals and performed his ablutions. He ordered that the gifts of the others be returned to them. Then Abdullah ibn Mas'ud hurried until he reached Badr, and he claimed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asked God's forgiveness for him when he heard of his death. This story was narrated on the authority of Ja'far and Umm Salamah may God be pleased with them, and its subject is the Book of the Seerah. The purpose is that the prophets (peace be upon them) continued to describe him and narrate it in their books to their nations, commanding them to follow him, support him, and stand by him when he is sent. The matter became famous among the people of the earth on the tongue of Abraham, the friend of God, the father of the prophets after him, when he prayed to the people of Mecca that God would send a messenger from among them, and likewise on the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary. For this reason they said: Tell us about the beginning of your matter, meaning on earth. He said: The supplication of my father Abraham, the good tidings of Jesus, son of Mary, and the vision that my mother saw. That is, the effect of that and the portent appeared among the people of Mecca, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it. And the Almighty said: But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, ‘This is obvious magic.’ Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Jarir said: But when he came to them Ahmad means the one given good tidings in ancient times, whose mention was mentioned in previous centuries. When his matter became apparent and he came with clear proofs, the disbelievers and opponents said, This is obvious magic.

That is, when they turned away from following the truth despite their knowledge of it, God caused their hearts to deviate from guidance and filled them with doubt, confusion, and failure, as God the Almighty said, And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression wandering blindly. And God the Almighty said, “And whoever contradicts the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.” For this reason, God the Almighty said in this verse, And God does not… He guides the wicked people. God the Almighty said: “And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, ‘O Children of Israel, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a Messenger to come after me, whose name is Ahmad.’” Meaning, the Torah gave good tidings of me, and I am the confirmation of what it had informed about, and I am the bearer of good tidings of the one who will come after me, who is the Messenger, the unlettered Arab Prophet from Mecca, Ahmad. So Jesus, peace be upon him, is the Seal of the Prophets of the Children of Israel, and he lived among the leaders of the Children of Israel giving good tidings of Muhammad, who is Ahmad, the Seal of the Prophets and Messengers, after whom there is no message or prophethood. How beautiful is the hadith that Al-Bukhari narrated in it, in which he said: Abu Al-Yaman told us, Shu’ayb told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im told me, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say, “I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi by whom God will wipe out disbelief, I am Al-Hashir, at whose feet mankind will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri, with a similar wording. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Al-Mas’udi told us on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abu Musa who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave himself names, some of which we have memorized. He said: I am Muhammad, and I am Ahmad, the Gatherer, the Returned, the Prophet of Mercy, Repentance, and the Great Battle. Muslim narrated it on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah with this same name. God the Almighty said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel (al-An’am 11:17). And God the Almighty said: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said: ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My covenant?’ They said: ‘We have acknowledged it.’ He said: ‘Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.’” Ibn Abbas said: God did not send a prophet without taking a covenant from him that if Muhammad were sent while he was alive, they would follow him, and he took a covenant from his nation that if Muhammad were sent while they were alive, they would follow him and support him. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to me on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma'dan on the authority of the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that they said: O Messenger of God, tell us about yourself. He said: “The supplication of my father Abraham and the good report of Jesus. My mother saw when she became pregnant with me as if a light had come out of her that illuminated the palaces of Busra in the land of Ash-Sham.” This is a good chain of narration, and corroborating evidence has been narrated for it from other sources. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, Muawiyah ibn Salih narrated to us on the authority of Saeed ibn Suwayd al-Kalbi on the authority of Abd al-A’la ibn Hilal al-Sulami on the authority of al-Arbadh ibn Sariyah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Indeed, I am the Seal of the Prophets in the sight of God, and Adam was still kneading in his clay. I will inform you of the beginning of that: the supplication of my father Abraham, the good report of Jesus, and the vision that my mother saw. And thus do the mothers of the prophets see.” Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, al-Faraj ibn Fadalah narrated to us, Luqman ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Umamah say: I said: O Messenger of God, what was the beginning of your affair? He said, "The supplication of my father Abraham and the good report of Jesus. My mother saw that a light came out of her that illuminated the palaces of Damascus." Ahmad also said: Hasan bin Musa told us, I heard Khadij, the brother of Zuhair bin Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent us to the Negus, and we were about eighty men, including Abdullah bin Masoud, Ja’far, Abdullah bin Rawahah, Uthman bin Maz’un, and Abu Musa. We went to the Negus and the Quraysh had sent Amr bin Al-’As and Ammarah bin Al-Walid with a gift. When they entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him, then they rushed to his right and left and said to him: Some of our cousins have settled in your land and have abandoned us and our religion. He said: Where are they? They said: They are in your land, so send for them. So he sent for them. Ja’far said: I am your orator today. They followed him and he greeted them but did not prostrate. They said to him: Why do you not prostrate to the king? He said: We do not prostrate except to God, the Almighty. He said: Why is that? He said: God sent His Messenger to us and he commanded us not to prostrate to anyone except God Almighty and he commanded us to pray and give zakat. Amr ibn al-'As said: They disagree with you about Jesus, son of Mary. He said: What do you say about Jesus, son of Mary, and his mother? He said: We say as God, the Almighty, said: He is the Word of God and His Spirit which He bestowed upon the pure Virgin, who was not touched by a human being and who did not have a son. He said: Then he picked up a stick from the ground and said: O people of Abyssinia, priests, and monks, by God, they do not add anything to what we say about him that is equal to this. Welcome to you and to those from whom you have come. I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God, and that he is the one we find in the Gospel, and that he is the one whom Jesus, son of Mary, gave good tidings of. Descend wherever you wish. By God, were it not for the kingdom I hold, I would have come to him and carried his sandals and performed his ablutions. He ordered that the gifts of the others be returned to them. Then Abdullah ibn Mas'ud hurried until he reached Badr, and he claimed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, asked God's forgiveness for him when he heard of his death. This story was narrated on the authority of Ja'far and Umm Salamah may God be pleased with them, and its subject is the Book of the Seerah. The purpose is that the prophets (peace be upon them) continued to describe him and narrate it in their books to their nations, commanding them to follow him, support him, and stand by him when he is sent. The matter became famous among the people of the earth on the tongue of Abraham, the friend of God, the father of the prophets after him, when he prayed to the people of Mecca that God would send a messenger from among them, and likewise on the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary. For this reason they said: Tell us about the beginning of your matter, meaning on earth. He said: The supplication of my father Abraham, the good tidings of Jesus, son of Mary, and the vision that my mother saw. That is, the effect of that and the portent appeared among the people of Mecca, so he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it. And the Almighty said: But when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, ‘This is obvious magic.’ Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Jarir said: But when he came to them Ahmad means the one given good tidings in ancient times, whose mention was mentioned in previous centuries. When his matter became apparent and he came with clear proofs, the disbelievers and opponents said, This is obvious magic.
61:7: God the Almighty says: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God while he is being called to Islam? That is, no one is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God and attributes to Him rivals and partners while he is being called to monotheism and sincerity. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. Then He the Almighty said: They want to extinguish the light of God with their mouths. That is, they try to repel the truth with falsehood, and their example in this is like someone who wants to extinguish the sun's rays with his mouth. Just as this is impossible, so is that impossible. For this reason, God the Almighty said: "And God will perfect His light, even though the disbelievers dislike it. It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it." We have already discussed these two verses in Surat Bara'ah sufficiently, and all praise and thanks are due to God.

61:10: It was mentioned in the hadith of Abdullah bin Salam that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, wanted to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the most beloved deeds to God Almighty for them to do, so God Almighty revealed this Surah and among its verses is this: O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a trade that will save you from a painful punishment? Then He explained this great trade that does not fail, which achieves the intended goal and removes the forbidden, so God Almighty said: “You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if you only knew.” That is, than worldly trade, toiling for it and dealing with it alone. Then God Almighty said: He will forgive you your sins. That is, if you do what I have commanded you to do and guided you to, He will forgive your mistakes and admit you to Paradise, good dwellings and high ranks. For this reason, God Almighty said: “And He will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and good dwellings in Gardens of Eden. That is the great attainment.” Then God Almighty said: And others that you love. That is, I will add to that for you. An increase that you love, which is Victory from God and an imminent conquest, meaning if you fight in His cause and support His religion, God will guarantee your victory. God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you and plant firmly your feet. And He the Almighty said: “And God will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.” And His saying: And an imminent conquest, meaning immediate. So this increase is the good of this world connected to the bliss of the hereafter for those who obey God and His Messenger and support God and His religion. For this reason, God the Almighty said: And give good tidings to the believers.

61:14: God Almighty says, commanding His believing servants to be supporters of God in all their circumstances, with their words, actions, selves, and wealth, and to respond to God and His Messenger, as the disciples responded to Jesus when he said: Who are my supporters to God? meaning who will help me in calling to God Almighty? The disciples said, and they were the followers of Jesus, peace be upon him, We are the helpers of God, meaning we are your helpers in what you were sent with and we will support you in that. For this reason, God sent them as missionaries to the people of the Levant, among the Israelites and the Greeks. Thus, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say during the days of Hajj: Who is the man who will shelter me so that I may deliver the message of my Lord? For the Quraysh have prevented me from delivering the message of my Lord. Until God Almighty sent for him the Aws and Khazraj of the people of Medina, so they pledged allegiance to him and supported him, and they stipulated that they would protect him from the blacks and the reds if he migrated to them. So when he migrated to them with his companions, they fulfilled their covenant with God. For this reason, God and His Messenger called them the helpers, and this became a symbol for them, may God be pleased with them and satisfy them. And the Almighty said: So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved meaning when Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, delivered the message of his Lord to his people and was supported by those who supported him from the disciples, a party of the Children of Israel was guided by what he brought them and a party went astray, so they deviated from what he brought them and denied his prophethood and accused him and his mother of grave sins. They are the Jews, upon them be the continuous curses of God until the Day of Resurrection. A party of those who followed him exaggerated regarding him until they raised him above what God had given him of prophethood and they split into sects and factions. Some of them said that he is the son of God, and some said that he is the third of three: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and some said that he is God. All of these statements are detailed in Surat An-Nisa. God the Almighty says: So We supported those who believed against their enemy, meaning, We granted them victory over the Christian sects who opposed them. So they became dominant, meaning, over them, through the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Imam Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu al-Sa`ib told me, Abu Mu`awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A`mash, on the authority of al-Minhal, meaning Ibn `Amr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When God the Almighty wanted to raise Jesus up to heaven, he went out to his companions, who were in a house with twelve men, from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water. He said: Among you is he who will disbelieve in me twelve times after having believed in me. He said: “Then he said: ‘Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him so that he may be killed in my place and be with me in my degree?’ He said: A young man, one of the youngest of them, stood up and said: “I will.” He said to him: Sit down. Then he repeated to them, and the young man...: Yes, you are that one. He said: So the likeness of Jesus was cast upon him, and Jesus, peace be upon him, was raised from a window in the house to heaven. He said: The demand came from the Jews, so they took his likeness, killed him, and crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after they had believed in him, so they split into three groups. One group said, God was with us as long as He willed, then He ascended to heaven. These are the Jacobites. One group said, The Son of God was with us as long as God willed, then He raised him to Him. These are the Nestorians. One group said, The servant and messenger of God was with us as long as God willed, then God raised him to Him. These are the Muslims. The two disbelieving women conspired against the Muslim woman, so they killed her. Islam remained obliterated until God sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So a party of the Children of Israel believed, and a party disbelieved. He meant the group of the Children of Israel who disbelieved during the time of Jesus and the group who believed during the time of Jesus. So We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became dominant. By Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, making their religion prevail over the religion of the disbelievers. This is his wording in his book when interpreting this noble verse. An-Nasa’i narrated it in the same way when interpreting this verse from his Sunan on the authority of Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah, with a similar wording. So the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will continue to be victorious upon the truth until God’s command comes and they are still like that, and until the last of them fights the Antichrist along with the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary (peace be upon him), as was mentioned in the authentic hadiths. And God knows best. End of the interpretation of Surat As-Saff. All praise and thanks are due to God.
